papers:

  # ─────────── direct-competitor ───────────

  - id: "libero_plus2025"
    title: "LIBERO-Plus: In-depth Robustness Analysis of Vision-Language-Action Models"
    authors: "OpenMOSS et al."
    venue: "arXiv (CVPR 2026 poster accepted)"
    year: 2025
    url: "https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.13626"
    category: "direct-competitor"
    role: "robustness benchmark + diagnosis baseline"
    relevance: "Most directly aligned prior work — defines 7 perturbation dimensions (object layout, camera, robot init, language, lighting, background, sensor noise) and shows VLA success drops 95→<30% under modest perturbations. Our PAR taxonomy (visual/spatial/physical) is a coarsening of theirs; we go beyond diagnosis to active correction via routed LoRA experts."
    key_findings: "Models exhibit extreme sensitivity to camera viewpoints + robot initial states; insensitive to language (ignore it). 10,030 tasks across 7 dimensions × 21 sub-dimensions with L1–L5 difficulty levels."

  - id: "robustvla2025"
    title: "RobustVLA: Robustness-Aware Reinforcement Post-Training for Vision-Language-Action Models"
    authors: "Anonymous et al."
    venue: "arXiv 2511.01331"
    year: 2025
    url: "https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.01331"
    category: "direct-competitor"
    role: "competing robustness post-training method"
    relevance: "Alternative path to VLA robustness — online RL with Jacobian + smoothness regularization. Differs from PAR: they modify the full policy via RL gradients; we keep π₀ frozen and add small targeted LoRAs. We should compare param count + need for env interaction."
    key_findings: "Jacobian regularization reduces sensitivity to observation noise; smoothness regularization stabilizes actions under perturbation. Online RL post-training framework."

  - id: "eva_vla2025"
    title: "Eva-VLA: Evaluating Vision-Language-Action Models' Robustness Under Real-World Physical Variations"
    authors: "Anonymous et al."
    venue: "arXiv 2509.18953"
    year: 2025
    url: "https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.18953"
    category: "direct-competitor"
    role: "robustness evaluation framework"
    relevance: "Frames physical variations as a continuous optimization problem to find worst-case perturbations. Reports >60% failure across all categories — motivates need for targeted correction (our PAR contribution)."
    key_findings: "Unified framework converting discrete physical variations into continuous optimization. Reveals significant fragility in current VLA systems."

  - id: "tt_vla2026"
    title: "On-the-Fly VLA Adaptation via Test-Time Reinforcement Learning"
    authors: "Anonymous et al."
    venue: "arXiv 2601.06748"
    year: 2026
    url: "https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.06748"
    category: "direct-competitor"
    role: "test-time adaptation baseline"
    relevance: "Alternative — adapt at test time via value-free PPO with progress rewards. Requires env interaction + reward signal. PAR is feed-forward: probe activation → route to expert, no online learning needed at deploy time."
    key_findings: "Within-episode policy adaptation via test-time PPO using dense progress-based rewards."

  - id: "preserve_pretrain2025"
    title: "Enhancing Generalization in Vision–Language–Action Models by Preserving Pretrained Representations"
    authors: "Anonymous et al."
    venue: "arXiv 2509.11417"
    year: 2025
    url: "https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.11417"
    category: "direct-competitor"
    role: "VLA generalization via representation preservation"

    key_findings: "Preserving pretrained VLM features improves OOD generalization vs aggressive full fine-tuning."

    title: "VLS: Steering Pretrained Robot Policies via Vision-Language Models"
    authors: "Anonymous et al."
    venue: "arXiv 2602.03973"
    year: 2026
    url: "https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.03973"

    key_findings: "Inference-time policy steering via VLM-derived trajectory-differentiable rewards, no policy parameter updates."
